7545-quotes-and-images-from-the-works-of:
This collection gathers quotations and images from Oliver Wendell Holmes Sr., and its editor's note begins by clearing up a common confusion. This is the physician and poet, not his son of the same name who became a Supreme Court Justice and famous in his own right. The elder Holmes became the editor's mentor in the philosophy of medicine, though his worldwide fame rested on prose and poetry.

The editor recalls assigning Holmes's Medical Essays to students whose sharp edges of science needed rounding off with a touch of humanity. That pairing, science with humanity, is the keynote of the quotations. Readers, especially any who may be physicians, are urged to meet Holmes the doctor-poet: witty, humane, and wise about the art that lies beside the science of healing.

govdocs-archive_org-nsia-SPSr_S_P_Sr:
Harold Weisberg wrote this note on February 11, 1992, about a strange phone call. A woman telephoned claiming to be Israeli intelligence. She identified a man in Warren Commission Exhibit 237 as a CIA assassin. She cited Peter Wyden's book 'Bay of Pigs' in support. Weisberg records that he doubted her story and saw no purpose for the call.

Old researchers attract strange callers, and Weisberg wrote them down like everything else. The note preserves the claim, the exhibit number, and his refusal to credit it. That refusal is the document's point. A man who spent thirty years accusing agencies still tested tips against evidence, and this one, in his judgment, failed the test on its face.
quotes-and-images-from-the-works-of-oliv:
Quotes and Images from Oliver Wendell Holmes, Sr. carries an editor's note by David Widger explaining that this Holmes is the physician and poet, not his son the Supreme Court justice. Holmes, Widger writes, was his mentor in the philosophy of medicine, and he once assigned the Medical Essays to students whose sharp science needed rounding with humanity.

The extracts that follow, in alphabetical order, keep the doctor-poet's wit. A misprint kills a sensitive author, absolute facts are bullies, and every literary man is advised to have a profession. All his geese are swans, one entry laughs, in a selection steeped in the talk of the breakfast table.
